question: Can sharper fixed-grid enclosure certify depth seven under the same budgets?

objects.domain: Uniform depths 6 and 7; fixed AW5 probes

objects.exact_expression: C^-_6=0.060216, C^-_7=0.020637 as outward lower bounds

sources.section_or_object_id: Recursive resolvent, local backward error and acquisition

Original timing, I/O, drift, operator and independent-noise budgets; each arm has gamma in [0,1/512]; binary64 normal arithmetic model

technique_plan.technique: Overlap bound, frequency conditioning and Gaussian Mills lower bound
technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: Sharpen numerical enclosure and disprove uniform depth-seven pass under original tolerances

calculation_steps: Bound repeated local corrections by maximum support multiplicity
Use high-frequency singular-value separation and a growing Fourier cutoff
Intersect per-arm intervals at the original damping endpoints
Construct allowed gains, offsets and Gaussian noise at depth seven

result.exact_expression: Depth-six lower bound 0.060216. Depth-seven undamped fixed-reference gap encloses [0.082828,0.086642], but an admissible Gaussian witness violates the uniform failure level under the original budget.
result.approximation: Depth-six headroom 0.013341; depth-seven alternative with sigma at most 1/128 has floor 0.047980
result.precision_and_error: Floors rounded downward; final common radius 0.000063 per arm plus weighted local residuals
result.scope: Uniform depths six and seven, original probes, no measured input

verification.method: Replay adaptive and legacy paths; rational threshold and Mills inequalities
verification.actual_result: PASS depth-six certificate, ideal depth-seven finite-window pass, and adverse Gaussian witness

counterexamples_and_failures: A legal pair of damping endpoints, signed gain/bias errors and independent Gaussian sample noise fails the depth-seven uniform probability target.
limitations: No hardware evidence or independent review.
Numerical enclosure assumes stated binary64 arithmetic model.
Sufficient quieter noise budget is a mathematical alternative.
changed_dependencies: Overlap aggregation replaces disjoint-child counting at each level for the new certificate.
next_discriminant: Derive a sharper noise or deterministic budget for the fixed-reference contrast and identify its spectral weight.
